To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the BMLD is reduced when the masker notch is wider and that this reduction can be accounted for by an adverse shift in interauaral phase in the across-channel process.
the BMLD decreases continuously as the notch-width increases and that this decrease cannot be explained by a model that does not include a detrimental across-channel effect.

the binaural notched-masker data are well predicted by a model that includes (1) a detrimental across-channel component that decreases with increasing frequency and (2) a nonlinear monaural frequency-selective component.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the auditory system processes the outputs of different auditory filters to obtain binaural information.

the question of whether binaural notched noise masking is based on a process that is limited to a single auditory filter or whether a process that involves more than one filter is required to explain the data.
the question of how the auditory system deals with binaural information in a noisy environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data are consistent with a model that includes a detrimental across-channel interaction, but the data do not allow a clear distinction between the two possible implementations of the model.
the binaural notched noise BMLD depends on the shape of the auditory filters, the interaural phase of the filters, and a detrimental across-channel effect.
the data are best accounted for by a nonlinear model that includes a detrimental process that operates across auditory channels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
binaural notched noise masking can be accounted for by assuming that binaural processing occurs after the auditory filters.
the BMLD is determined by the interaction of a binaurally specific process that is tuned to interaural phase, and an across-channel process that is tuned for interaural level differences.
the binaural auditory system processes the output of more than one auditory filter, and this processing is frequency dependent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the shape of the auditory filter is not the sole determinant of the BMLD.

the BMLD is not a simple measure of interaural phase discrimination, but that it is affected by the processing of the auditory filters that are adjacent to the filter centered at the frequency of the signal.

binaural masking-level differences for notched-noise masks cannot be explained by models that do not consider a detrimental across-channel effect, even when the model includes a nonlinear frequency selectivity and interaural differences.
